Package io.github.mikestitt.corbelsflightlog

Class FlightLog

java.lang.Object
io.github.mikestitt.corbelsflightlog.FlightLog
public final class FlightLog extends Object
One WPILOG file per OpMode run, for AdvantageScope.

Files are named <run>-<date>-<time>.wpilog in directory (logs by default). On an FTC robot, corbelsflightlog-ftc points that at /sdcard/FIRST/logs. Open the files with AdvantageScope.

Only changes are written. Each channel remembers the last value it wrote and skips a call whose value is identical. AdvantageScope holds a value until the next record, so nothing is lost -- a boolean that's true for the whole match is one record, not one per loop. The exception is event(java.lang.String), which records every call, since two identical events are two things that happened.

Never throws into the OpMode. If the file can't be opened or a write fails, logging switches itself off and status() says why.

One type per channel. A channel's type is fixed by its first value. A later call with a different type is ignored, and a one-time note is added to /Events so it's easy to spot.

Pose frame. Pose methods take Pedro coordinates (inches, origin in a field corner, radians) and write WPILib Pose2d structs in the frame AdvantageScope's FTC fields use: meters, origin at field center, turned by fieldQuarterTurns -- VERIFY that turn for your season.

  • Field Details

    • directory

      public static File directory
      Where log files go. Public so tests can point it at a temp folder.

    • fieldQuarterTurns

      public static int fieldQuarterTurns
      Counter-clockwise quarter turns from Pedro's axes to AdvantageScope's FTC axes. UNVERIFIED for BIOBUZZ: 1 is what another team used for DECODE's layout. Display only -- nothing on the robot reads it.

      public String status()

    • number

      public void number(String key, double value)
      A double. NaN and infinities are skipped (a gap in the graph).

    • float32

      public void float32(String key, float value)
      A float, stored as a 4-byte float so 0.1f reads as 0.1. Deliberately not an overload of number(java.lang.String, double): Java would pick a float overload for an int argument, silently storing number("x", 5) as a float.

    • integer

      public void integer(String key, long value)
      An integer: counts, encoder ticks, states as numbers.

    • bool

      public void bool(String key, boolean value)
      A true/false: limit switches, "has game piece", "at speed".

    • text

      public void text(String key, String value)
      Text, e.g. a state name. null is written as "null".

    • pose

      public void pose(String key, double xIn, double yIn, double headingRad)
      A Pedro pose, drawn on AdvantageScope's 2D field.

    • poses

      public void poses(String key, double[] xyh)
      Several Pedro poses -- a path, a list of targets -- as one Pose2d[], which AdvantageScope draws as a trajectory. The array is {x0, y0, heading0, x1, y1, heading1, ...} in Pedro inches and radians. An empty array clears it. Skipped if any value is non-finite.

    • numbers

      public void numbers(String key, double[] values)
      Several doubles as one value, e.g. four motor powers.

    • integers

      public void integers(String key, long[] values)
      Several integers as one value, e.g. four encoder positions.

    • integers

      public void integers(String key, int[] values)
      Same as integers(String, long[]), for int[].

    • bools

      public void bools(String key, boolean[] values)
      Several true/falses as one value, e.g. which of three slots are full.

    • event

      public static void event(String message)
      Records a one-off event in the current log's /Events channel, with its exact time. Every call is recorded, even a repeat. Callable from anywhere -- OpModes, subsystems, commands. Does nothing if no log is open.

    • endLoop

      public void endLoop()
      Call once per loop. Flushes to storage about once a second.

    • close

      public void close()
      Flushes and closes the file. Safe to call more than once.
